trends.whatProductOffers: A qualifying deferred annuity policy that converts savings into a level monthly annuity payment over a 10-year annuity period, with the guaranteed portion starting at a chosen age of 50, 55, 60, 65, 70 or 75.

keyFigures.label: Premium payment term
keyFigures.condition: annuity can start as early as the 6th year

exclusionsOrConditions: Only the guaranteed portion of the monthly annuity payment is guaranteed; the non-guaranteed portion depends on divisible surplus and may be zero.
The 10-year annuity period is fixed; the brochure excerpt does not describe a lifetime annuity option.
The annuitant must be the insured and is the person receiving the payment.
Guaranteed cash value reduces once the guaranteed monthly annuity payment begins.
clientSignalPhrases: needs to cover daily expenses in retirement
wants level income, not lump sum
negativeSignalPhrases: wants a lump sum at retirement
clientProfileFit: Clients converting a maturing savings policy

trends.whatProductOffers: The client can take the monthly annuity payment in cash or leave it to accumulate in the policy for potential interest, and can change the annuity payment option without an additional charge.

exclusionsOrConditions: Accumulated payments may earn interest at rates determined by the company; the rate is not stated in the excerpt.

The 5-year premium term is the only term described in the excerpt; other terms may exist but are not in the text.

trends.whatProductOffers: As a Qualifying Deferred Annuity Policy, premiums can be tax deductible up to HK$60,000 per taxpayer per year where the annuitant is the taxpayer or their spouse and that person has taxable income in the year.

keyFigures.label: Tax deduction cap
keyFigures.value: Up to HK$60,000 per taxpayer each year

keyFigures.label: Eligibility condition
keyFigures.value: Annuitant must be the taxpayer or the taxpayer's spouse
keyFigures.condition: with taxable income in the taxation period

exclusionsOrConditions: Deduction requires the annuitant to be the policyholder or spouse and to have taxable income during the taxation period.
The HK$60,000 is a deduction cap, not a tax credit; the tax saved depends on the marginal rate.
Tax rules can change; the brochure directs clients to the IRD and their own tax advisers.
The deduction is per taxpayer per year, not per policy.
clientSignalPhrases: high earner, wants to reduce tax
wants tax planning before year end
needs the deduction and retirement income
negativeSignalPhrases: has no taxable income in Hong Kong
wants the annuitant to be a child
expects a tax credit rather than a deduction
clientProfileFit: Clients already using voluntary MPF contributions
trends.talkingPointTemplate: For {client_detail}, the QDAP status allows up to HK$60,000 of premium per taxpayer per year to be deducted, provided the annuitant is the client or spouse with taxable income.
verificationPrompts: Confirm the client's and spouse's taxable income and existing QDAP deductions.
Confirm the annuitant meets the QDAP eligibility condition.

sourceEvidence: "AIA Deferred Annuity Plan 2 is a Qualifying Deferred Annuity Policy (\"QDAP\")"
"Tax deduction of up to HK$60,000 per taxpayer each year (if eligible)"
trends.notesForReviewer: Tax treatment depends on IRD rules at the time of assessment.

trends.whatProductOffers: The plan includes a Terminal Illness Benefit paying a one-off advance, and an Unemployment Benefit that extends the premium payment period from 31 days up to 365 days.

keyFigures.label: Unemployment Benefit
keyFigures.value: Premium payment period extended by 31 to 365 days

exclusionsOrConditions: The terminal illness advance is subject to certification and reduces policy values; the excerpt does not state the advance amount.
The unemployment extension is a deferral of premium, not a waiver; missed premiums remain payable later.
Both benefits are subject to the policy's terms and conditions, which are not fully reproduced in the excerpt.
